speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any difficulty swallowing or pain when eating? I also need to know if you have experienced any changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea or constipation.

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: I noticed an enlarged supraclavicular lymph node during my exam; have you felt any lumps in your neck, armpits, or groin? REQUEST TEST: CT Scan of Abdomen and Pelvis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Scan of Abdomen and Pelvis: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Splenomegaly detected. Dullness noted over the left lower quadrant.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Patient
text: I have smoked about one pack a day for many years, and I drink socially. The abdominal discomfort and fatigue have both been getting worse. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: CT Scan of Chest. Do you have any persistent cough or shortness of breath?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Scan of Chest: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the smoking history and massive lymphadenopathy, I need to rule out lung cancer versus lymphoma. REQUEST TEST: CT-guided biopsy of mediastinal lymph node.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Biopsy of cervical lymph node reveals lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results showing CD20-positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index are diagnostic for a B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, most likely Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL). DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
